findings.title: Charge expiry omits the reached end-of-action clear for remaining count 1
findings.behavioral_fact: Charge starts at 2. Normal round-tail processing can reduce it to 1. Reaching the end-of-action cleanup clears exactly count 1 before later Instruct/Dancer processing; count 2 is not cleared by that action cleanup. The clear is not conditional on having used an Electric move or on successfully dealing damage.
prerequisites: Default Charge was successfully used; no special ability/item/state callbacks alter the counter.
Both sides remain able to battle; a later ordinary move attempt reaches its normal end-of-action cleanup.

For the repeat example: a legal positive-PP ordinary Electric move is in the user’s current slots, normal gates pass, and a later ally uses legal Instruct after the user’s ordinary action; no special blacklist, locks, switching, fainting or host fault applies.
findings.minimal_counterexample: Charge succeeds in round n: counter 2, then full round-tail 1. In round n+1 the user performs its normal Electric move: its initial damage reads positive Charge and receives the Charge power multiplier. The normal action end clears counter 1 to 0. A later ally’s Instruct repeats that Electric move in the same round, so the repeat reads 0 and receives no Charge multiplier. A timer-only implementation inferred from WP44 keeps 1 through both actions until the round tail and boosts the repeat incorrectly.
findings.ordinary_control: Immediately after newly setting Charge to 2, reaching that same action’s end leaves it 2; this is distinct from the count-1 clear. Another independent control removes Instruct and still observes the counter clear after the ordinary action.
findings.cancellation_or_partial_commitment: Successful first damage, PP and history stay committed; a later repeat does not undo them. A failed ordinary attempt that reaches the same end cleanup also clears the remaining count. A fault or branch that does not reach the cleanup has no automatic clear guarantee.
findings.needed_consumer: The exact end-of-action count-1 clear is needed in addition to WP43’s positive-count multiplier and WP42’s decrement; current WP40 mentions only an unspecified charge-remnant cleanup.

negative_searches.result: WP44 body fully read; catalog fully read; focused cross-owner search found establishment, positive power multiplier, tail decrement, and WP40’s unspecific cleanup label, but no explicit count-1 clear or repeat regression.

findings.minimal_revision: Add the reached action-end rule: if remaining Charge is exactly 1, clear it before later repeated-move consumers. Keep the existing 2 establishment, tail decrement, failure-stage and execution caveats. Name the exact rule at WP40’s cleanup handoff.
preserved_scope: No new Charge duration or persistent field design.
No change to the default positive Charge multiplier or round-tail decrement.
No claim about runtime media, host recovery, or every exceptional callback.
acceptance_regression: Reached ordinary action cleanup changes 1 to 0 regardless of move type or damage success.
A successful Electric move then same-round legal Instruct has Charge multiplier only on the first use.
An earlier fault that does not reach action cleanup is a separately conditional case.
dependencies: WP40 reached action cleanup and repeat execution
findings.rebuttal_target: Show an existing frozen formal clause that already defines exactly 1→0 before repeated-move consumers, or show the legal repeat cannot occur under the listed conditions.

findings.title: Fang status immunity short-circuits the status random draw before the flinch draw
findings.behavioral_fact: Once a Fang secondary callback is actually reached and its internal chance is positive, it queries status eligibility first. Only an eligible status consumes its own status draw. The subsequent flinch draw is separate and still occurs when status is ineligible; it occurs before the Inner Focus rejection at flinch submission. The outer secondary-effect gate is a separate earlier draw; the default Thunder Fang outer chance is 101.
prerequisites: Default Thunder Fang with ordinary command/PP/target checks passing.
The damage route reaches the secondary callback: calculated damage positive, no Sheer Force suppression, no active Shield Dust unless ignored, no substitute absorption.
Current mechanics use Electric-type paralysis immunity; actual target is pure Electric, remains alive, has no Inner Focus and no callback altering the status eligibility or counter.
No additional chance modifiers: internal chance 10. All earlier accuracy/critical/variance/outer draws fixed separately; the next two available internal random values are 5, then 99.
findings.minimal_counterexample: Against an Electric target, paralysis eligibility is false before any status random draw. The first available internal random value 5 is consumed by flinch, so Flinch becomes true; 99 is not consumed inside that Fang callback. Reading “separately draw for status and flinch” as an unconditional pair instead consumes 5 on an impossible paralysis and 99 on flinch, producing false and shifting later random consumers.
findings.ordinary_control: With an otherwise identical target that is not paralysis-immune, internal 5 produces paralysis, then internal 99 does not flinch. If status submission immediately cures the new status, that submission and its cure callbacks still happened before the flinch draw. Another independent control has active Inner Focus: the flinch draw is still consumed, but its commit is rejected.
findings.cancellation_or_partial_commitment: The hit’s damage/PP/history are already committed before the internal callback. Immunity cancels only the status branch’s draw/commit, not the subsequent flinch draw. Status application and immediate cure are not rolled back by a later failed flinch commit.
findings.needed_consumer: Conditional random-consumption order needs the actual status query before the draw and the flinch commit after its own draw; two independent marginal chances alone do not define the sequence.

negative_searches.result: Full assigned formal text has two separate draws and component immunity, but does not specify the status-eligibility short circuit or a Fang internal random-consumption vector.

findings.minimal_revision: Qualify the Fang rule: query the chosen status first and draw its internal roll only if eligible; then independently draw for flinch and apply flinch’s own commit guard. Keep the distinct outer secondary gate and chance modifiers.
preserved_scope: No claim that all secondary effects share Fang’s draw order.
No change to the 10% internal base chances or ordinary chance modifiers.
No runtime or global replay claim.
acceptance_regression: Reached callback with status eligible: next internal 5,99 applies status, no flinch; two draws.
Reached callback with status immune: next internal 5,99 flinches; one internal draw, 99 remains for later consumer.
Positive chance and Inner Focus: draw consumed but flinch not committed.
Substitute, zero internal chance, or outer suppression skips the respective callback/draw path.
dependencies: WP43 probability helper and outer gate
WP44 status eligibility and flinch commit
findings.rebuttal_target: Demonstrate that the frozen formal wording already fixes conditional draw consumption, or that the listed default Thunder Fang callback cannot be reached.

findings.title: Psycho Shift uses generic status eligibility and bypasses sleep/freeze clause wrappers
findings.behavioral_fact: Psycho Shift target eligibility calls the generic status query directly. The rule module adds Sleep Clause/Modified Sleep Clause and Freeze Clause only to the dedicated sleep/freeze queries, not to that generic query. Sleep Talk can legally choose Psycho Shift and calls it through the special route, allowing an actually sleeping user to reach the transfer.
prerequisites: Sleep Clause or Modified Sleep Clause is enabled and no later plugin replaces these queries.
User is sleeping with remaining count 2 before its ordinary Sleep Talk check; Sleep Talk reduces it to 1 but remains usable while asleep.
User knows legal Sleep Talk plus Psycho Shift; Psycho Shift is the only eligible called candidate, no contrary slot restrictions, no no-PP Sleep Talk failure.

Opposing target is alive, raw status NONE, with a different opposing non-egg party member already sleeping. Generic status guards pass: no substitute/protection, terrain/Uproar/status immunity, Prankster Dark restriction, reflection or callback affecting this example.
The target submission’s random sleep duration and any later cures are fixed separately; no held cure/ability cure exists in the minimal vector.
findings.minimal_counterexample: The already sleeping opposing party member makes an ordinary direct sleep effect fail the dedicated Sleep Clause query. Under the same opposing party state, Sleep Talk calls Psycho Shift: generic status eligibility accepts the empty-status target, the target receives a newly chosen sleep duration, and the user is then cured. The same wrapper bypass exists structurally for transferring frozen status, without claiming a default ordinary frozen-user route.
findings.ordinary_control: Keep the target’s generic guards and party state identical, but use ordinary SleepTarget through its dedicated sleep query: the clause rejects it and no target sleep is committed. Independently clear the existing opposing sleep: dedicated sleep and the generic transfer can both pass their respective queries.
findings.cancellation_or_partial_commitment: Sleep Talk’s own PP and its initial sleep decrement are prior commitments. Called Psycho Shift uses special usage and does not consume a persistent Psycho Shift slot’s PP through the simple new-move route. Target status submission and its reactions precede the user cure; later cure/failure does not imply no target submission occurred.
findings.needed_consumer: The clause-wrapper consumer boundary must be distinguished from the generic eligibility used by Psycho Shift; declaring only “target must accept status” leaves the exception unresolved.

negative_searches.result: WP44 body/effect coverage and full shared catalog freshly read; focused formal search found generic Psycho Shift acceptance plus ordinary clause descriptions, but no explicit Psycho Shift generic-query exception or regression.
Fresh exact-range inspection found wrappers for dedicated sleep, Yawn, freeze; no generic-query clause wrapper in the inspected rule block.

findings.minimal_revision: State in Psycho Shift’s bounded rule that it uses generic status eligibility and does not inherit the dedicated sleep/freeze clause wrapper. Add the ordinary direct sleep versus Sleep Talk→Psycho Shift control, leaving generic immunity/terrain/protection unchanged.
preserved_scope: Retain specialized clause behavior on ordinary dedicated sleep/freeze and Yawn.
Do not assert all forced calls or debug submissions bypass all guards.
Do not invent a default frozen-user route.
acceptance_regression: Enabled Sleep Clause, opposing reserve asleep, empty target: ordinary direct sleep rejected.
Same state, eligible Sleep Talk calls Psycho Shift: user sleep 2→1, target new sleep, user cured; outer PP remains spent.
Added generic terrain or immunity gate rejects transfer while keeping earlier Sleep Talk/PP commitments.
Target immediate cure case still registers the prior submission and subsequent user cure.
dependencies: WP44 generic status query and clause entry boundaries
WP47-A Sleep Talk pool and special call
WP40 special usage skip and PP/history
WP46/50 immediate cures and stage commitment
findings.rebuttal_target: Show an existing frozen formal exception for Psycho Shift’s clause-wrapper bypass or prove the listed ordinary Sleep Talk pool rejects Psycho Shift.
